intro: Find what is trending, compare the market, decide whether to sell (or undercut) or promote as an affiliate, and write your own scripts from winning patterns. Researched 2026-10-08 by seven agents.

pipeline.summary: A weekly n8n-orchestrated pipeline can run the research with Google Sheets as the datastore and Claude for normalization and script drafting, at roughly $5-60/month in tools plus optional Keepa/Kalodata subscriptions. Official APIs cover search demand (YouTube, Google Ads keyword ideas, Google Trends alpha), prices/fees (Amazon Creators API, SP-API fees, eBay Browse, SerpApi, Keepa) and EU-only ad libraries (Meta, TikTok), but the highest-signal sources for US short-form ads and TikTok Shop products (TikTok Creative Center, Meta Ad Library UI for US commercial ads, Kalodata/FastMoss) have no open API and need a 15-30 minute manual export or Apify scrapers that conflict with platform ToS. The scoring model weights demand growth 30%, margin/commission 25%, competition 20%, ad saturation 15%, affiliate availability 10%, with hard gates and an undercut formula that subtracts fees, CPA and returns. Humans must set up accounts and API approvals once, approve every 'sell' decision and every script (FTC disclosure, claims, originality) before hand-off to posting automation. Schedule: Weekly, Monday 06:00 local (n8n Schedule Trigger); review window Mon-Tue; posting Wed-Sun.

steps.name: Collect trend signals (Mon 06:00)
steps.inputs: category watchlist (Sheet tab config), keyword seeds, last week's products tab
steps.tools: API: YouTube Data API, Google Ads KeywordPlanIdeaService, Google Trends API alpha (if granted), Keepa best sellers, Meta Ad Library API (EU/UK), TikTok Commercial Content API (EU), Reddit API; manual export: TikTok Creative Center Top Products/Top Ads, Kalodata/FastMoss CSV, Meta Ad Library UI (US), Pinterest Trends, Google Trends CSV if no API; scraper fallback ToS risk: Apify actors for Creative Center / TikTok Shop / Amazon movers
steps.outputs: raw signal: signal_id, run_id, collected_at, source, source_type(api|manual|scraper), region, raw_product_title, category_hint, metric_name, metric_value, period_days, url, ad_id(optional)
steps.human: Create accounts/keys once; do 15-30 min manual exports Monday morning into manual_import tab; approve list of allowed scrapers.
steps.cost: $0-15 (Apify usage if used; Keepa sub is monthly)
steps.cautions: YouTube 10k units/day; Sheets 60 writes/min/user; Keepa token bucket; TikTok/Meta/Amazon ToS prohibit scraping - prefer API/manual.

steps.name: Normalize and score shortlist
steps.tools: LLM: Claude Haiku: cluster titles into canonical products (JSON schema); compute: n8n Code node calculates sub-scores
steps.outputs: product: product_id, run_id, canonical_name, category, signal_count, sources[], demand_growth_pct, search_volume, video_views_30d, competition_sellers, ad_advertisers_30d, est_price, est_landed_cost, est_margin_pct, affiliate_available, best_commission_pct, score_demand, score_competition, score_margin, score_saturation, score_affiliate, total_score, status
steps.human: Review the weights in config tab once; spot-check merged clusters weekly.
steps.cautions: Anthropic API rate limits by tier; batch 50 titles per call.

steps.name: Market comparison and undercut check (top 20 by total_score)
steps.tools: API: SerpApi Google Shopping, eBay Browse API, Amazon Creators API / Keepa, AliExpress Affiliate API (supplier cost), Amazon SP-API Product Fees; manual: Meta Ad Library UI longest-running ads, TikTok Shop listing check
steps.outputs: comparison: product_id, competitor_name, channel, price, rating, review_count, shipping_days, active_ads_count, longest_ad_days, offer_angle; undercut: product_id, market_p25_price, market_median_price, our_target_price, landed_cost, platform_fees, est_cpa, unit_profit_at_target, undercut_feasible(bool), differentiation_ideas[]
steps.human: Confirm landed cost from real supplier quote before any 'sell' decision.
steps.cautions: SP-API fees 1 req/s; SerpApi free 250/mo; eBay call limits.

steps.name: Decide sell vs affiliate
steps.tools: compute: rules in n8n Code node; LLM: Sonnet writes 3-line rationale
steps.outputs: decision: product_id, path(sell|affiliate|skip), expected_profit_per_sale, expected_commission_per_sale, capital_required, risk_flags[], rationale
steps.human: Human approves every 'sell' (inventory risk); affiliates can be auto-approved if commission >= threshold.

steps.name: Draft original scripts from patterns
steps.inputs: approved decisions, pattern library (abstracted hooks/structures from top ads), product facts sheet, Reddit pain points
steps.outputs: script: script_id, product_id, path, pattern_used, hook, body_beats[], cta, on_screen_text[], duration_s, disclosure_text, claims[], claim_evidence[], similarity_check_passed, status=drafted
steps.human: Maintain product facts and allowed claims; never supply competitor scripts verbatim.
steps.cautions: Prompt includes rule: do not reproduce text from any real ad; LLM similarity check vs stored ad metadata.

steps.name: Human review
steps.tools: tools: Google Sheets review_queue view, Slack/Gmail notification from n8n, n8n Wait node resume webhook
steps.outputs: review: script_id, reviewer, decision(approved|edit|rejected), edited_script, compliance_checklist{disclosure,claims_substantiated,no_fake_testimonial,no_copied_copy}, approved_at
steps.human: Mandatory: reviewer checks FTC disclosure, claims, originality, platform ad policy.

steps.name: Hand off to posting automation
steps.inputs: approved scripts, affiliate links / product page URLs
steps.tools: tools: n8n webhook to existing posting automation (Bundlepad posting tab), Google Drive folder for briefs
steps.outputs: handoff: script_id, product_id, platforms[], asset_brief, caption, hashtags[], link, disclosure_text, schedule_at, utm_campaign, status=queued
steps.human: Human records/edits video or approves AI video; posting tool credentials configured.
steps.cautions: Each platform's posting API limits and branded-content toggles (TikTok/Instagram paid-partnership labels).

pipeline.scoring: Normalize each metric to 0-100 within this week's candidate set (percentile rank) unless an absolute cap is given., D = demand score: 0.5*pct_rank(demand_growth_pct) + 0.3*pct_rank(video_views_30d) + 0.2*pct_rank(search_volume)., C = competition score (inverse): 100 - pct_rank(competition_sellers) (Keepa/eBay/Shopping seller counts)., M = margin score: sell path -> clamp(est_margin_pct/40*100, 0, 100) (40% net margin = full marks); affiliate path -> clamp(commission_per_sale_usd/10*100,0,100)., S = ad saturation (inverse): 100 - clamp(ad_advertisers_30d/50*100,0,100); +10 bonus (cap 100) if longest-running competitor ad > 30 days (proof the angle sells) but advertisers < 20., A = affiliate availability: 100 if program with >= 10% commission, 60 if 5-10%, 30 if < 5%, 0 if none., TOTAL = 0.30*D + 0.20*C + 0.25*M + 0.15*S + 0.10*A., Gates (hard filters before scoring): signal_count >= 2 distinct sources; no restricted category (supplements health claims, weapons, IP-branded knockoffs); est_price >= $15., Shortlist = TOTAL >= 60, max 20 per week; tune weights in config tab after 4-6 weeks using actual results.

sources.name: TikTok Creative Center - Top Ads
sources.what_it_shows: Best-performing TikTok ads with filters for region, industry, objective, ad format (Spark / non-Spark), language, likes band and period (7/30/180 days). You can sort by For You, Reach, CTR, 2s and 6s view rate, CVR and likes. CTR is shown as a percentile within the industry (e.g. 'Top 10%'), not a raw rate. The detail view adds a second-by-second engagement and drop-off timeline, keyframe analysis and the landing page.
sources.has_api: No official API for Top Ads. Third-party Apify actors scrape it (unofficial).
sources.account_needed: Free TikTok for Business account to see full filters and details. Some lists are browsable logged out. No ad spend required.
how_to_use: 1. Log in at ads.tiktok.com/business/creativecenter and open Inspiration > Top Ads Dashboard.
2. Set Region (e.g. US), Industry (e.g. Beauty & Personal Care), Objective = Conversions or Product Sales, Period = Last 7 days.
3. Sort by CTR, then separately by CVR, and note ads that rank high on both.
4. Open each ad's Details. Note the hook in the first 3 seconds, where the engagement timeline peaks and drops, the CTA timing and the landing page.
5. Log the ad into your swipe file (product, angle, hook type, length, CTR percentile, format).
6. Repeat for 2-3 adjacent industries and regions such as UK, CA and AU to find products that cross markets.
sources.agent_can_automate: Partly. There is no API, so an agent can drive a logged-in browser session or use a paid third-party scraper. Copying data by hand into a spreadsheet works reliably. Judging the creative stays human or needs a vision model.
sources.terms_notes: TikTok's terms restrict automated scraping, and third-party scrapers carry ToS and account risk. Data covers ads TikTok chooses to feature, not all ads. Ad assets are copyrighted: study the patterns, do not reupload.
sources.best_for: Fastest free view of which TikTok ad creatives and hooks are winning right now by industry and region.

details.ctr_display: percentile vs industry, not raw rate

sources.name: TikTok Creative Center - Top Products
sources.what_it_shows: Products ranked by how their ads perform on TikTok, filterable by region, category and period (1/7/30 days). Product detail shows popularity, CTR, CVR, CPA, an impressions trend chart and the top ads for that product.
sources.has_api: No official API.
sources.account_needed: Free TikTok for Business account.
how_to_use: 1. Open Creative Center > Inspiration > Top Products.
2. Choose the region and a product category. Set the period to 7 days, then 30 days, to compare.
3. Sort by popularity change and CTR. Flag products with rising impressions and above-median CVR.
4. Click Details to see the impressions trend and the linked top ads.
5. Cross-check each flagged product on Amazon Movers & Shakers and Google Trends (see those sources) before deciding to source it, undercut it or promote it as an affiliate.
sources.agent_can_automate: Partly. An agent can do a weekly browser-assisted export into a sheet. Deciding which product to pursue stays human.
sources.terms_notes: Categories are broad product types (e.g. 'Skincare tools'), not specific SKUs or brands. Metrics come from ad data, not sales. Region coverage varies.
sources.best_for: Spotting product categories whose TikTok ads are gaining traction, before you go looking for suppliers or affiliate offers.

sources.name: TikTok Creative Center - Trends (Hashtags, Songs, Creators, Videos)
sources.what_it_shows: Trending hashtags, songs, creators and organic videos by region and industry. Hashtags show popularity over time, the audience's age and interests, and related videos. Songs can be filtered to those approved for business use and show an analytics curve. Creators are ranked by followers and engagement per region.
sources.has_api: No official API. Partial organic data is available through the TikTok Research API, but only for approved academic researchers.
sources.account_needed: Browsable logged out in many regions. A free TikTok for Business account unlocks more filters.
how_to_use: 1. Open Creative Center > Trends and pick Hashtags, Songs, Creators or TikTok Videos.
2. Set Region and Industry, and Period = 7 days. Turn on 'New to top 100' to catch breakout trends.
3. For songs, tick 'Approved for business use' so you can legally use the audio in ads.
4. Open the analytics for each trend and check that the curve is rising rather than peaked.
5. Note which product categories appear in the top videos for each hashtag.
sources.agent_can_automate: Partly. Weekly screenshot or browser capture works. Third-party scrapers exist but are unofficial.
sources.terms_notes: Organic trend data only, with no sales or ad metrics. Commercial audio use is limited to the business-approved music library.
sources.best_for: Timing: which sounds and hashtag formats to wrap your product ad in this week.

sources.name: TikTok Creative Center - Keyword Insights
sources.what_it_shows: Keywords and phrases used in TikTok ad scripts, ranked by popularity, CTR, CVR, CPA and 6s view rate. Filters cover region, industry, objective, keyword type (selling points, pain points, audience, CTAs, product) and time. The data comes from ads, not organic posts.
sources.has_api: No official API.
sources.account_needed: Free TikTok for Business account.
how_to_use: 1. Open Creative Center > Keyword Insights.
2. Filter Region + Industry + Objective = Conversions.
3. Switch Keyword Type through Pain points, Selling points and CTAs. Sort by CTR and CVR.
4. Click a keyword to see example ads using it and the trend over time.
5. Build a phrase bank of pain point, benefit and CTA words, and use it to write original scripts.
sources.agent_can_automate: Partly. Browser capture into a phrase-bank sheet works. Writing the scripts can be automated with an LLM, as long as it follows your own originality rules.
sources.terms_notes: Ad-derived data. Keyword type names may change. Region availability varies.
sources.best_for: Learning the wording that converts (pain points, benefits, CTAs) in a niche so you can write your own scripts.

sources.name: TikTok Commercial Content Library + Commercial Content API
sources.what_it_shows: A searchable library of ads shown in the EU/EEA (plus Switzerland and the UK, per TikTok's library pages) with advertiser, first and last shown dates, targeting parameters, the number of unique users reached (ranges) and removed ads. Ads stay searchable until one year after they were last shown. It does not include CTR or spend.
sources.has_api: Yes. The Commercial Content API (query ads by advertiser name or keyword). Access requires a TikTok for Developers account plus an application that is reviewed in about 1-2 weeks.
sources.account_needed: TikTok for Developers account using an official email, plus an approved Commercial Content API application. The web library (library.tiktok.com) needs no account.
how_to_use: 1. Web: open library.tiktok.com/ads, pick an EU country and date range, and search a competitor brand or keyword.
2. Open each ad to see its reach range, targeting and run dates. Long-running ads are likely profitable.
3. API: register at developers.tiktok.com, apply for the Commercial Content API, and describe your use case honestly.
4. Once approved, use the client key to get a client-credentials token, then call the ad query endpoint with search terms, country and date filters.
5. Store the results and rank advertisers by how many ads they run and how long the ads stay live.
sources.agent_can_automate: Yes for the API once approved, including scheduled queries on competitor names and keywords. The web library is manual.
sources.terms_notes: Coverage is EU/EEA (and UK/CH per TikTok) only; US-only ads are not included (unverified whether this has expanded by 2026). Approval is discretionary and terms limit use to the stated purpose.
sources.best_for: Checking whether a competitor or brand is actively scaling TikTok ads and for how long.

sources.name: TikTok Research API
sources.what_it_shows: Public organic video data: video metadata, views, likes, shares, comments, hashtags, music and user info. It is query-based.
sources.has_api: Yes, but restricted to approved non-profit academic researchers in eligible regions (US, EEA, UK, CH and others). Not available for commercial use.
sources.account_needed: Academic institution affiliation plus an approved research application.
how_to_use: 1. Check eligibility. Businesses and marketers are not eligible.
2. If you are not eligible, use the Creative Center Trends pages or a compliant third-party data vendor instead.
sources.agent_can_automate: No for commercial users.
sources.terms_notes: Commercial use is prohibited and data-handling rules are strict. Listed here so the guide does not suggest it as a route for sellers.
sources.best_for: Explaining why you cannot pull TikTok organic video data officially for business use.

sources.name: Meta Ad Library (web)
sources.what_it_shows: All active ads running across Facebook, Instagram, Messenger and Audience Network in every country. You see the creative, copy, start date, platforms, number of ad versions and the landing link. Ads delivered in the EU also show EU reach, age/gender/location breakdowns and the payer. Political and issue ads show spend and impression ranges. Commercial ads show no spend, CTR or likes.
sources.has_api: Partial. The web UI covers all active commercial ads worldwide, but the API (see next entry) returns commercial ads only if they delivered in the EU.
sources.account_needed: None to search. A Facebook login sometimes helps avoid limits.
how_to_use: 1. Open facebook.com/ads/library, set Country = United States (or your market) and Ad category = All ads.
2. Search a product keyword (e.g. 'posture corrector') or a competitor page name.
3. Filter Active status = Active. Sort or scan by start date: ads running 30+ days, with many versions, are likely winners.
4. Click 'See ad details' and note the number of versions (more variations usually means the advertiser is scaling).
5. Visit the landing page to log price, offer, bundle and guarantee. This is your undercut baseline.
6. Save the patterns (hook, format, offer) to your swipe file, never the ad files themselves.
sources.agent_can_automate: Partly. A browser agent can search and summarize. Bulk access is only through the API (EU data) or third-party tools.
sources.terms_notes: Meta prohibits automated scraping without permission. Inactive non-political ads disappear from the library. Longevity and version count are proxies for performance, not real metrics.
sources.best_for: Finding competitor ads that have run for weeks or months (a sign of profitability) in any country.

sources.name: Meta Ad Library API
sources.what_it_shows: Programmatic search (Graph API ads_archive endpoint) of political and issue ads globally, plus all ads delivered in the EU (and associated territories). Commercial ads return creative text, links, delivery dates, EU reach and demographic breakdowns. Spend and impressions are returned only for political ads.
sources.has_api: Yes. The ads_archive Graph API endpoint. Requires a Meta developer account, identity confirmation and an app with an access token.
sources.account_needed: A Facebook account with confirmed ID, Meta for Developers app and access token.
how_to_use: 1. Confirm your identity at facebook.com/ID and create an app at developers.facebook.com.
2. Generate a user access token in the Graph API Explorer.

3. Call GET /ads_archive with search_terms, ad_reached_countries (e.g. ['DE','FR']), ad_type=ALL, ad_active_status=ACTIVE, and fields such as ad_creative_bodies, ad_delivery_start_time, page_name, eu_total_reach, ad_snapshot_url.
4. Page through the results and store them in a database. Rank by eu_total_reach and days active.
5. Re-run weekly to detect new creatives from tracked competitors.
sources.agent_can_automate: Yes for EU-delivered commercial ads and political ads. No for US-only commercial ads.
sources.terms_notes: Commercial ads that ran only in the US or other non-EU markets are not returned. Rate limits apply. Platform terms restrict how data is used.
sources.best_for: Automated weekly tracking of competitor ad volume and creative changes in the EU market.

sources.name: Google Ads Transparency Center
sources.what_it_shows: Ads from verified advertisers across Search, YouTube, Display, Shopping/Maps and Play. Filters cover advertiser or domain, region, date and format (text, image, video). Shows the creative, first and last shown dates and regions. For EU, it adds impression ranges and targeting. No CTR or spend for commercial ads.
sources.has_api: Partial. There is no official REST API for commercial ads. Google's political ads data is in a public BigQuery dataset. A BigQuery dataset for EEA creative stats is reported by third parties (unverified). Third-party scrapers exist.
sources.cost: Free (BigQuery queries are billed per bytes scanned beyond the free tier of 1 TB/month)
sources.account_needed: None for the web. A Google Cloud project for BigQuery.
how_to_use: 1. Open adstransparency.google.com and search a competitor domain (e.g. example-brand.com).
2. Set Region and Format = Video to see their YouTube ads, or Text to see their Search ad copy.
3. Note how long each creative has been shown. A long-running Search headline usually means a proven offer.
4. For YouTube video ads, open the creative and note the hook and offer structure.
5. Optional: in BigQuery, search the public datasets for 'ads transparency' and query EU creative stats if the dataset is available (unverified).
sources.agent_can_automate: Partly. The web is manual or uses a browser agent. BigQuery is automatable if the dataset is confirmed.
sources.terms_notes: Google ToS restricts scraping. Commercial impression data covers the EU only. Coverage is limited to verified advertisers.
sources.best_for: Seeing a competitor's Search copy and YouTube video ads by domain.

sources.name: LinkedIn Ad Library
sources.what_it_shows: Ads run on LinkedIn in the last 12 months, searchable by advertiser, keyword, country and date. Shows the creative, copy, CTA and format. EU-served ads add impression ranges, impressions by country and targeting parameters.
sources.has_api: No official public API (unverified). Third-party Apify scrapers exist.
sources.account_needed: None to browse.
how_to_use: 1. Open linkedin.com/ad-library and search a keyword or competitor company.
2. Filter by country and date range (last 30 days).
3. Open the ads and, for EU ads, check the impression ranges to see which creatives got volume.
4. Log offers and lead-magnet angles. This is mainly relevant to B2B products, courses and SaaS affiliates.
sources.agent_can_automate: Partly. A browser agent or third-party scraper. Impressions load after the page renders, so a full browser is needed.
sources.terms_notes: LinkedIn strictly prohibits scraping in its User Agreement and has pursued legal action over scraping.
sources.best_for: B2B, SaaS and course affiliate niches.

sources.name: YouTube Charts and Explore (replaces Trending page)
sources.what_it_shows: YouTube retired the Trending page and Trending Now list in July 2025. It was replaced by category charts (Trending Music Videos, Top Podcast Shows, Trending Movie Trailers, Gaming Explore) and the Explore menu. These show organic popularity, not ads.
sources.has_api: No for the charts site. Use the YouTube Data API mostPopular chart (next entry).
sources.account_needed: None.
how_to_use: 1. Open charts.youtube.com and pick a country and chart.
2. For product research, search YouTube for '<product> review' and 'TikTok made me buy it', sort by upload date or view count, and note recent videos with outsized views.
3. Check YouTube Shorts in your niche for formats that are crossing over from TikTok.
sources.agent_can_automate: Partly. Use the Data API search and video lists instead of the charts site.
sources.terms_notes: The general Trending page no longer exists, so older guides referring to it are out of date.
sources.best_for: Long-form review and 'haul' content that shows which products buyers are researching.

sources.name: YouTube Data API v3 (videos.list chart=mostPopular, search.list)
sources.what_it_shows: The most popular videos by region (regionCode) and category (videoCategoryId), with view, like and comment counts, publish date, tags and duration. search.list finds videos by keyword, ordered by viewCount or date.
sources.has_api: Yes. YouTube Data API v3 with an API key from Google Cloud.
sources.cost: Free within quota. The default is 10,000 units/day. videos.list costs about 1 unit per call. search.list costs 100 units per call. Extra quota requires an audit application.
sources.account_needed: A Google Cloud project with YouTube Data API v3 enabled and an API key.
how_to_use: 1. Create a Google Cloud project, enable YouTube Data API v3 and create an API key.
2. Call GET videos?part=snippet,statistics&chart=mostPopular&regionCode=US&videoCategoryId=26 (Howto & Style) or 22, 24, etc. Get category IDs with videoCategories.list.
3. For product keywords: search?part=snippet&q=<product>+review&order=viewCount&publishedAfter=<30 days ago>&type=video, then videos.list on the IDs to get statistics.
4. Compute views per day since publish and flag outliers.
5. Store results weekly to see momentum.
sources.agent_can_automate: Yes. This is a fully official API and a good candidate for scheduled agents.
sources.terms_notes: The YouTube API Services Terms require refreshing or deleting stored data after 30 days in many cases. The mostPopular chart skews toward entertainment. Keyword search is the better route for products.
sources.best_for: Automated, official data on which product review videos are gaining views.

sources.name: Pinterest Trends (web) + Pinterest Trends API
sources.what_it_shows: Pinterest search-term trends by region, with weekly, monthly and yearly growth, filters for interests, age and gender, and top Pins per term. Trend types include growing, monthly, yearly and seasonal. Strong signal for home, decor, fashion, beauty, DIY and gifts.
sources.has_api: Partial. The Pinterest API v5 'List trending keywords' endpoint (GET /trends/keywords/{region}/top/{trend_type}) returns up to 50 keywords with WoW, MoM and YoY growth for today's date only. Access is limited and needs app review.
sources.account_needed: Free Pinterest business account for the web tool. A developer app plus approved access for the API.
how_to_use: 1. Log in with a business account at trends.pinterest.com.
2. Choose Region and Trend type = Growing trends, and filter by interest (e.g. Home decor).
3. Click a term to see its yearly curve and top Pins. Plan products 6-8 weeks ahead of seasonal peaks.
4. API (if approved): GET /v5/trends/keywords/US/top/growing?interests=home_decor and store the results daily, since there is no history in the API.
sources.agent_can_automate: Partly. The API is automatable if access is granted. Otherwise use a browser agent.
sources.terms_notes: Trends API access is restricted and not widely available. The API returns no historical data.
sources.best_for: Spotting seasonal and lifestyle product demand early, especially for women 25-44 shoppers.

sources.name: Google Trends + Google Trends API (alpha)
sources.what_it_shows: Relative search interest (0-100) over time by region and sub-region, related queries and topics (rising and top), and a YouTube Search and Google Shopping filter. 'Trending now' shows real-time breakout searches. The API alpha (launched July 2025) gives consistently scaled data over a rolling 5-year window with daily, weekly, monthly and yearly aggregation.
sources.has_api: Partial. The Google Trends API is in alpha and limited to approved testers through an application form. There is no official API otherwise. pytrends-style libraries are unofficial.
sources.account_needed: None for the web. Apply at developers.google.com/search/apis/trends for the API.
how_to_use: 1. Open trends.google.com/explore, enter up to 5 product terms and set Country and Past 12 months.
2. Switch the search type to Google Shopping or YouTube Search to see buyer intent.
3. Check 'Related queries > Rising' for breakout sub-products and modifiers (e.g. 'for dogs', 'cordless').
4. Compare a candidate product against a stable benchmark term so you can read scale.
5. A rising 90-day slope plus a TikTok Top Products signal means stronger demand; a sharp spike that is already decaying means you are late.
6. API: apply for alpha access. If approved, schedule weekly pulls of your watchlist terms.
sources.agent_can_automate: Partly. Yes through the alpha API if approved. Otherwise a browser agent or the CSV download button.
sources.terms_notes: Values are relative, not absolute volumes. Unofficial scrapers are often rate-limited or blocked (HTTP 429).
sources.best_for: Validating that a TikTok-viral product has real, growing search demand and isn't a one-week spike.

sources.name: X (Twitter) Ads Repository
sources.what_it_shows: A DSA compliance repository of ads served in the EU: advertiser, funding entity, targeting parameters, impressions and reach, and halted ads. Search results have historically been delivered as CSV/Excel exports.
sources.has_api: No (as of mid-2026). In July 2026 X committed to the European Commission to add an API, show results in the interface and include the full ad content and destination URLs (status unverified).
sources.account_needed: None, or an X account, depending on the current UI (unverified).
how_to_use: 1. Open the ads repository page, select an EU country and enter an advertiser handle.
2. Request or download the CSV of ads for the date range.
3. Sort by impressions to find the creatives that got the most delivery.
sources.agent_can_automate: Partly. CSV parsing is automatable. The request step is manual until the API ships.
sources.terms_notes: EU only. In December 2025 X was fined EUR 120M under the DSA, partly over shortcomings in this repository. It is a low priority for e-commerce research.

frameworks.name: Swipe-file to original script workflow
steps: Collect 20-50 winning ads in your niche (Creative Center, Meta Ad Library, Kalodata, PiPiAds) - prefer ads running 30+ days or with high revenue.
Tag each: hook type, angle (pain, desire, curiosity), format (UGC talking head, demo, unboxing, green screen, before/after), length, offer, CTA.
Count which tags repeat most - that is the pattern, not any single ad.
Write your own script using the pattern + your product's real USP, your own words and your own footage.
Make 3-5 hook variants per body; test with small budgets; keep winners, kill losers in 48-72h.
Run each script through the compliance checklist (FTC, platform policy, copyright).
frameworks.example: Pattern found: 7 of 10 top desk-organiser ads open on a messy-to-tidy reveal under 2 s and end with a bundle offer. Original script: [0-2s] hand sweeps clutter into a drawer that clicks shut - 'Thirty seconds. That's all my desk gets now.' [2-15s] show three compartments, cable slot, magnet lid. [15-22s] 'Two-pack is cheaper than one at the mall.' [CTA] 'Grab the bundle from the orange cart.'

steps: Call-out: name the audience ('Night-shift nurses...').
Bold claim/result (provable only).
Curiosity gap / open loop ('I didn't expect the cheap one to win').
Problem shown visually (spill, tangle, mess).
Pattern interrupt (unexpected motion, prop, sound).
Question ('Why does your phone die by 3pm?').
Negative/warning ('Stop buying refill pads until you see this').
Social proof (real number: 'Our 2,000th order shipped today').
frameworks.example: 'If your dog treats your sofa like a napkin, watch this.' (on screen: dog wipes face on a cover, owner peels it off and tosses it in the wash)

frameworks.name: 3-second hook rules
steps: Movement or a face in frame 0.
On-screen text that restates the hook (many watch muted).
Show the product or the problem within 2 s.
No logo intro or slow pans.
Measure: 3-second view rate / thumb-stop rate (aim to beat your account average; >25-30% is commonly cited as good, unverified).
frameworks.example: Frame 0: close-up of cold coffee being poured out. Text: 'Never microwaving coffee again.' Voice: 'This mug keeps it hot for three hours.'

frameworks.name: Problem-Agitate-Solution (PAS)
steps: Problem: state the pain plainly.
Agitate: make the cost of the pain concrete.
Solution: product as relief, with proof (demo).
CTA.
frameworks.example: P: 'Charging cables everywhere?' A: 'Three chargers, still hunting one at midnight.' S: 'One stand, three devices, one cable.' CTA: 'Tap to get yours.'

frameworks.name: Before-After-Bridge (BAB)
steps: Before: life with the problem.
After: life without it (realistic, not exaggerated).
Bridge: the product is how you get there.
Avoid body/weight before-after (restricted on TikTok/Meta).
frameworks.example: Before: 'Sunday used to be three hours of meal prep.' After: 'Now it's forty minutes and I'm on the couch by noon.' Bridge: 'This stackable container set with the portion lids.'

frameworks.name: AIDA
steps: Attention: hook.
Interest: surprising feature or fact.
Desire: benefit + proof + social proof.
Action: clear CTA with offer/urgency that is true.
frameworks.example: A: 'This flashlight is also a power bank.' I: 'Charges your phone twice.' D: 'Fits in a glovebox, waterproof, real buyer reviews on screen.' A: 'Weekend price ends Sunday - link below.'

frameworks.name: UGC testimonial format
steps: Use a REAL customer or a creator who actually received and used the product.
Selfie-style, natural light, talk to camera.
Structure: hook -> my problem -> what I tried -> this product -> results I saw -> who it's for -> CTA.
Disclose: #ad / Paid partnership if creator was compensated or got free product.
Never script false results or invented personas.
frameworks.example: Creator (gifted product, disclosed): 'I've tried four pillow sprays and this is the first one my partner didn't complain about. Lavender, not perfume-y. It's in my cart now - #ad.'

frameworks.name: Demo / 'show don't tell'
steps: Lead with the most visual feature.
One feature per 3-5 s cut.
Use real-time (uncut) demo for credibility.
End on the result shot + CTA.
frameworks.example: 0-3s: knife sharpener, dull tomato squish. 3-10s: five pulls through the sharpener. 10-15s: same knife glides through tomato. Text: 'Five pulls.' CTA: 'Shop now.'

frameworks.name: CTA patterns
steps: Direct: 'Tap Shop Now' / 'Tap the orange cart'.
Offer-led: 'Bundle saves 20% today' (must be true).
Low-friction: 'See colours' / 'Check if it fits your car'.
Affiliate: 'Link in bio - I earn a small commission'.
Repeat CTA in on-screen text and caption.
frameworks.example: 'Check the two-pack price - it's in the yellow basket below. (I get a commission if you buy.)'

frameworks.name: Length norms (TikTok/Reels/Shorts)
steps: TikTok in-feed direct response: 9-15 s for simple impulse products; 21-34 s often cited as TikTok's sweet spot (originates from a 2021 organic-video finding, not hard ad data).
Reels: 15-30 s; Stories 5-15 s.
YouTube Shorts ads: under 60 s, keep 15-30 s.
Test 3 lengths of the same script (short/medium/long) rather than trusting benchmarks.
frameworks.example: Cut A 12 s (hook + demo + CTA), Cut B 24 s (adds 2 real reviews), Cut C 35 s (adds problem story). Same hook, compare CPA.

frameworks.name: Undercut / affiliate decision from ad research
steps: For each winning product: note retail price in ads, number of active advertisers, ad run length, TikTok Shop affiliate commission.
If many sellers + high commission -> affiliate route (make your own video, earn commission, no inventory).
If few sellers, high price, cheap supplier -> own store at lower price or better bundle, with your own creatives.
Differentiate on offer (bundle, warranty, faster shipping) not on copying their ad.
Never use their brand name, logo or trademarked product name in your ad.
frameworks.example: Competitor sells a heated eye mask at $39 with 12 active ads; supplier cost $8; TikTok Shop commission 15%. Options: affiliate at ~$5.85/sale, or own listing at $29 + free travel pouch with your own unboxing demo.

frameworks.name: Compliance checklist per script
steps: All claims true and substantiated?
Any testimonial from a real user, with consent and disclosure?
Material connection disclosed (#ad, affiliate)?
No personal-attribute call-outs (Meta) or body shaming / weight before-after (TikTok)?
All footage, music, fonts owned or licensed?
No competitor trademark/footage?
Urgency/discount real?
frameworks.example: Flagged: 'Are you diabetic? This tea fixes it.' -> rewrite: 'A caffeine-free evening tea with no added sugar.'

frameworks.name: Landed cost per unit
steps: L = unit_cost + inbound_freight_per_unit + duty + broker_fees_per_unit + prep_packaging_per_unit + inspection_per_unit
duty = customs_value_per_unit x (base_HTS_rate + additional_tariff_rate)  (customs_value usually FOB price)
inbound_freight_per_unit = total_freight_quote / units  (or by volume share: freight_total x unit_cbm / total_cbm)
Dropship variant: L = supplier_price + supplier_shipping_to_customer (+ duty if not DDP); ship_cost below = 0 because supplier ships
frameworks.example: Factory $4.00 FOB, freight $0.90/unit, duty 4.00 x 0.30 = $1.20, prep $0.40 -> L = $6.50.

frameworks.name: Per-platform fee functions F(P, S) where P = item price, S = shipping charged
steps: Amazon FBA: F = max(r_cat x (P+S), 0.30) + fba_fee_tier (+ monthly storage share). r_cat = 0.15 most.
TikTok Shop: F = r_tt x (P+S) + c_creator x P + fbt_fee. r_tt = 0.06 (stress-test 0.08), c_creator seller-set e.g. 0.15.
Etsy: F = 0.20 + 0.065 x (P+S) + (0.03 x (P+S) + 0.25) [+ 0.15 x (P+S) capped 100 if Offsite Ads sale]
eBay: F = 0.136 x (P+S+tax) + (0.30 if P+S <= 10 else 0.40) [+ promoted_rate x (P+S)]
Shopify Basic: F = 0.029 x (P+S) + 0.30 + plan_monthly / orders_per_month + apps_monthly / orders_per_month
Walmart: F = r_wm x (P+S) + wfs_fee (r_wm 0.06-0.20)
Generic: F = pct x (P+S) + fixed_per_order
frameworks.example: Etsy $20 item + $5 shipping: 0.20 + 1.625 + 1.00 = $2.83 fees.

frameworks.name: Contribution margin and break-even ROAS / CPA
steps: Revenue R = P + S
CM_pre_ads = R - L - ship_cost - F(P,S) - return_rate x (L_lost + return_ship) - payment/other variable
CM% = CM_pre_ads / R
Break-even ROAS = R / CM_pre_ads = 1 / CM%
Break-even CPA = CM_pre_ads (max ad spend per order before loss)
Target ROAS = R / (CM_pre_ads - target_profit_per_order)
Profit per order at actual ROAS = CM_pre_ads - R / ROAS
Markup <-> margin: margin = markup / (1 + markup); markup = margin / (1 - margin)
frameworks.example: R $30, L $6.50, ship $5, fees $3.90, returns $0.60 -> CM $14.00 (46.7%) -> BE ROAS 2.14, BE CPA $14.00; for $5 profit target ROAS = 30/9 = 3.33.

frameworks.name: Minimum viable price (solve for P)
steps: Let all percentage costs on revenue be p_total = platform_pct + creator_pct + payment_pct + returns_pct + ad_pct, where ad_pct = 1 / planned_ROAS
Let all fixed per-order costs be C_fixed = L + ship_cost + fixed_fees + packaging
Require profit margin m on revenue: P_min = C_fixed / (1 - p_total - m)
Valid only if p_total + m < 1; otherwise product cannot work at that ROAS
If shipping is charged separately, solve for R and subtract S
frameworks.example: C_fixed $11.80, platform 6% + creator 15% + returns 3% + ads 1/3 (ROAS 3) = 57.3%, m = 10% -> P_min = 11.80 / 0.327 = $36.12.

frameworks.name: Undercut test vs a competitor offer
steps: Competitor effective price E = (price + shipping - coupon/discount) / units_in_bundle
Your effective price Y = (P + S - discount) / your_units
Candidate undercut P_u = E x (1 - u) with u e.g. 5-10%, or E - $1
Undercut is viable if P_u >= P_min and CM at P_u gives BE ROAS <= the ROAS you can realistically get (assume 1.5-2.5 for cold traffic)
If not viable: change offer instead of price (bundle 2-pack, faster shipping, better warranty) - compare value not price alone
Price-war guard: if competitor's 90-day Keepa low < P_min, do not enter on price
frameworks.example: Competitor $34.99 free ship; P_min $36.12 -> straight undercut fails; sell a 2-pack at $54.99 ($27.50/unit) where L doubles but shipping/fees per order stay ~flat.

frameworks.name: Offer comparison score (rank competing offers)
steps: Collect for each offer: effective unit price E, rating r (1-5), review_count n, delivery_days d, bundle/extras, return policy
Price score = min_E / E
Trust score = (r / 5) x min(1, log10(n+1) / 3)  (1,000 reviews = full credit)
Speed score = min(1, 3 / d)  (3 days or faster = 1)
Total = 0.40 price + 0.30 trust + 0.20 speed + 0.10 extras (0-1 judged)
Your offer must beat the leader on total, not only on price; weights editable
frameworks.example: Leader $30, 4.5 stars, 2,000 reviews, 2 days vs you $27, 0 reviews, 7 days: you win price but lose trust and speed - fix by US warehouse and seeding reviews via creators.

frameworks.name: Affiliate vs sell decision
steps: Affiliate earnings per sale A = price x commission_rate (TikTok creator commission or Amazon Associates rate)
Seller profit per sale = CM_pre_ads - ad_cost_per_order
Affiliate has no inventory, refund or IP risk; choose affiliate when A >= 50% of seller profit or when you lack capital/brand rights
Choose sell/undercut when you can reach P_min below market and own the listing (private label or authorized)
frameworks.example: $30 item at 15% creator commission = $4.50 per sale risk-free vs ~$5 seller profit after ads with inventory risk -> start as affiliate, switch if volume proves out.

frameworks.name: MAP / trademark risk gate
steps: Is the item a branded product? Check USPTO and Amazon Brand Registry signals.
If yes and you are not authorized: do not list it as that brand; build an unbranded/private-label equivalent with your own photos and copy.
If authorized reseller under MAP: advertised price must be >= MAP; undercut only via bundles/value if policy allows.
Never reuse competitor images, video, or ad script text; model the pattern only.
Avoid patented designs (search Google Patents for design patents).
frameworks.example: A trending branded massage gun: sell an unbranded equivalent from a factory with your own name and photos, not the brand's listing.

frameworks.name: Undercut feasibility check
steps: market_p25_price = 25th percentile of competitor prices across Amazon/Shopping/eBay/TikTok Shop.
our_target_price = market_p25_price * 0.95 (or match p25 with a differentiator such as bundle/faster shipping).
unit_profit = target_price - landed_cost - platform_fees - payment_fees - est_cpa - returns_allowance(5% of price).
undercut_feasible = unit_profit >= max($5, 20% of target_price).
If not feasible -> try affiliate path; if no affiliate >= 5% -> skip.
frameworks.example: p25 $29.99 -> target $28.49; landed $7.80, fees $5.40, CPA $9, returns $1.42 -> profit $4.87 -> below $5 floor -> choose affiliate at 15% ($4.27/sale, no inventory) or skip.

frameworks.name: Sell vs affiliate decision rules
steps: If undercut_feasible and capital_required <= budget and supplier sample approved -> sell.
Else if affiliate commission_per_sale >= $3 and program allows paid ads/organic content you plan -> affiliate.
Else if both possible: pick higher expected_profit_per_sale x estimated conversions, penalizing sell by 20% for inventory risk.
Otherwise skip and keep on watchlist 4 weeks.
frameworks.example: Desk organizer: sell profit $8.10 vs affiliate $2.40 -> sell, pending sample.

frameworks.name: Pattern-to-original-script method
steps: Extract only structure from top ads: hook type (problem callout, before/after, demo, contrarian), length, beat order, CTA type, visual style.
Store patterns as abstract labels, never the ad text.
Feed LLM: pattern label + your product facts + allowed claims + disclosure rule.
Generate 3 variants with different hooks; run similarity check against stored competitor captions; reject > 0.8 similarity.
Human edits for voice and compliance.
frameworks.example: Pattern 'problem callout -> 3-second demo -> one proof point -> CTA'. Draft: 'Cables everywhere on your desk? This clips under in ten seconds. Holds six cords, no tools. Link below - I earn a commission if you buy.'

frameworks.name: Weekly cross-source trend sweep (agent plan)
steps: Agent A (TikTok): pull Top Products (7d) and Top Ads sorted by CTR and CVR for 3 target categories in the US. Log the top 20 products and the hooks of the top 10 ads.
Agent B (search demand): for each product, query Google Trends (12 months, Shopping) and the YouTube Data API (review videos from the last 30 days). Tag each as Rising, Flat or Spiking-decaying.
Agent C (market proof): check Amazon Movers & Shakers and Best Sellers for the product. Record price, rating, review count and the top 3 complaints.
Agent D (competition): search the Meta Ad Library (US, active) for the product keyword. Count advertisers and ads running 30+ days, and note the price and offer on each landing page.
Score each product on demand trend, ad proof, competition count, margin room and complaint-fixability. A human picks: affiliate, undercut, improved version or skip.
frameworks.example: Product: cordless mini massager. TikTok Top Products shows impressions up week over week, Google Shopping interest is rising, it is #14 on Amazon Movers & Shakers at $39 with a 4.1 rating and battery complaints, and 9 Meta advertisers have ads running 30+ days. Decision: source a longer-battery version priced at $34 and lead with the battery angle.

frameworks.name: Ad pattern teardown (study patterns, write your own)
steps: Pick 5 ads with high CTR percentiles or long run times in the same niche.
For each ad, label the hook type (problem callout, shocking demo, before/after, 'I tried X', price reveal), the length, the second when the product appears, proof elements and the CTA wording.
Use the TikTok engagement timeline to note where viewers drop off.
Find the pattern shared by 3 or more ads. That is the format to test.
Write 3 original scripts using that pattern, your own product angle and wording drawn from Keyword Insights and Reddit pain-point language. Never reuse their footage, voiceover or exact lines.
frameworks.example: Pattern: a 2-second visible problem, the product fixing it within 4 seconds, then a price anchor. Original script: 'My desk cables looked like spaghetti. [snap the clip on] Thirty seconds, done. Ten clips for less than a coffee - link below.'

frameworks.name: Late-or-early check
steps: Compare the TikTok Top Products 7-day vs 30-day popularity.
Check the slope of the Google Trends 90-day curve.
Count new Meta advertisers that started in the last 14 days.

If interest is rising and the advertiser count is still low, you are early: test it. If interest is flat or falling and many advertisers are running, the market is saturated: promote it as an affiliate or skip it.
frameworks.example: Rising Trends slope plus 3 Meta advertisers means early, so test a $50 ad budget. A flat slope plus 40 advertisers means saturated, so skip it or promote it only as an affiliate.

frameworks.name: Trend-to-margin funnel
steps: Spot: pull risers from Amazon Movers & Shakers, TikTok Creative Center Top Products, Kalodata/FastMoss 7-day growth, Exploding Topics.
Confirm demand: Google Trends 5-year line (not a one-week spike), Semrush/Ahrefs volume and CPC, Keepa rank stable or improving 30+ days.
Measure competition: number of sellers (Keepa/Walmart report), review counts, eBay sell-through.
Price the undercut: AliExpress/Alibaba unit cost + shipping + duty + marketplace fees + ad cost per sale vs current selling price.
Decide path: margin >30% after ad cost -> sell; otherwise -> affiliate (Amazon Associates, TikTok Shop affiliate, AliExpress Portals, Walmart/eBay affiliate).
frameworks.example: A collapsible silicone kettle shows up on Movers & Shakers 4 days running, Keepa rank improves for 6 weeks, Google Trends rising. Sells at $34; AliExpress cost $9 + $5 shipping + ~$5 fees = $19, leaving $15 before ads. If test ads cost under $8 per sale, sell it; if not, promote the Amazon listing as an affiliate.

frameworks.name: Cross-platform price comparison table
steps: For each candidate, record: Amazon price/rank (Creators API or Keepa), eBay avg sold price (Product Research), Etsy price range (Open API), TikTok Shop GMV and price (Kalodata), AliExpress cost and commission (affiliate API), Walmart presence.
Flag gaps: high price on one platform vs low cost on AliExpress = undercut opportunity; product absent from a platform = expansion gap.
Rank by (price - landed cost) x demand score.
frameworks.example: Row: 'LED pet collar' - Amazon $22 (rank 1,800 in Pet), eBay sold avg $15, TikTok Shop $19 with $40k 7-day GMV, AliExpress $3.10 at 7% commission; not sold on Walmart -> candidate to list on Walmart and eBay at $17.

frameworks.name: Agent automation plan for this research
steps: Agent 1 (daily): Keepa bestsellers + product endpoints for 10-20 target categories; store rank deltas.
Agent 2 (daily): AliExpress hotproduct.query for matching categories; store cost and commission.
Agent 3 (weekly): Google Merchant Center Best Sellers BigQuery table; eBay Browse API price spread; Etsy listings scan.
Human (weekly): export Kalodata/FastMoss top products and TikTok Creative Center Top Products (no API), drop CSVs in a folder for the agents.
Agent 4: merge into one comparison sheet, compute margin and demand score, shortlist top 10 with links to the top-selling videos for ad-pattern study.
frameworks.example: Monday report: '3 new risers in Kitchen; best margin: magnetic spice rack ($27 Amazon vs $6 AliExpress, rank up 40% in 14 days); top TikTok video uses a before/after clutter reveal in the first 2 seconds.'

frameworks.name: Affiliate vs undercut decision
steps: Find a trending product (TikTok Shop sales, Amazon Movers & Shakers).
Look up the same item via eBay Browse API, Awin/CJ feeds, AliExpress API for landed cost.
Compute affiliate earnings per sale = price x commission.
Compute own-sell margin = price - (supplier cost + shipping + marketplace fees + ad cost per sale).
If margin < 2x affiliate earnings or brand is trademarked/patented, choose affiliate; otherwise test selling.
frameworks.example: A $30 posture corrector pays 15% on TikTok Shop ($4.50). AliExpress landed cost $7, fees ~$5, ads ~$9: own-sell margin ~$9. Affiliate first to validate, then sell a bundled variant.

frameworks.name: Program stacking per product
steps: Check if the product is on TikTok Shop (highest rate).
Else Amazon or Walmart Creator link.
Add YouTube Shopping tag for long-form.
Track per-link EPC in a sheet weekly.
frameworks.example: Video on TikTok uses showcase link; same review on YouTube tags the Amazon listing; blog links Walmart where cheaper.

frameworks.name: Disclosure template
steps: Say it in the first seconds of the video.
Write it next to the link.
Turn on platform paid-partnership label.
frameworks.example: Spoken: 'Heads up, I earn a small commission if you buy through my link.' Caption: '#ad - commission link below.'

rules: Learn from winning ads (hooks, structure, angles), then write your own script. Never copy another ad's words, footage or music: that is copyright infringement and gets ads rejected.
Prefer official APIs, exports and ad libraries. Scraping TikTok, Meta or Amazon breaks their terms; use manual exports where no API exists.
Disclose affiliate links and paid promotion clearly in the post itself (#ad, "Paid partnership", "I earn a commission").
No fake reviews, fake testimonials or made-up results. Health, money and before/after claims need proof and are restricted on every platform.
Check trademarks and brand rules before selling or undercutting: no knock-offs of branded products, and respect MAP (minimum advertised price) agreements where you have one.

summaries.m1_trend_ads: The richest free source of ad performance signals is the TikTok Creative Center. Top Ads shows CTR and CVR percentiles, Top Products shows product-level ad performance, Keyword Insights shows the wording that converts, and Trends covers hashtags, songs and creators. None of these have an official API. Ad transparency libraries (Meta, Google, LinkedIn, TikTok, Snap, X) show which creatives are running and for how long, but not CTR or spend for commercial ads. Their APIs mostly cover only EU-delivered ads because of DSA rules. For US commercial ads, run time and number of variations in the Meta Ad Library are the main performance signals. For demand, the official automatable sources are the YouTube Data API, Google Trends (API in limited alpha since July 2025) and the Pinterest Trends API (restricted access). Amazon Best Sellers and Movers & Shakers confirm actual sales and give the price baseline for an undercut. A practical agent plan combines these in a weekly sweep: TikTok signals, then search demand, then Amazon proof, then Meta competition.
summaries.m2_products: Free marketplace lists (Amazon Best Sellers / Movers & Shakers, eBay Product Research, Google Merchant Center Best Sellers, TikTok Creative Center Top Products, Walmart best sellers) show what is selling now at no cost. For real numbers and automation, the best APIs are Keepa (Amazon rank/price history, from EUR 49/mo), Amazon Creators API (replaced PA-API 5 in 2026; needs active Associates sales), AliExpress affiliate API (hot products + commissions, supplier cost), eBay Browse API and Etsy Open API v3 (free). TikTok Shop sales estimates come from paid tools (Kalodata, FastMoss, Shoplus ~$40-130/mo; EchoTik cheapest and has an API). Exploding Topics, Glimpse, Google Trends and Semrush/Ahrefs confirm whether demand is rising. Most third-party sales figures are estimates and 2026 prices come largely from third-party trackers, so verify before buying.
summaries.m3_affiliate: Most marketplaces where trending products sell run affiliate programs, so you can earn without inventory. TikTok Shop and YouTube Shopping pay merchant-set rates (commonly 10-20%) on in-app sales, while Amazon pays 1-10% by category (with unannounced 2026 cuts) and requires 3 sales in 180 days. Networks with real APIs (eBay Browse API, Awin, CJ, Impact, AliExpress, Amazon Creators API once eligible) let agents pull live prices and generate links, enabling automated price comparison to decide affiliate vs undercut. Digital-offer networks (ClickBank, Digistore24) pay 50-75% but carry compliance risk. Every affiliate post must carry a clear FTC disclosure near the link and in the video.
summaries.m4_scripts: Free official ad libraries (TikTok Creative Center, Meta Ad Library, Google Ads Transparency Center) show which ads run longest and which keywords/hooks drive CTR; paid spy tools (Foreplay, Atria, Minea, PiPiAds, BigSpy, AdSpy, Kalodata) add search, tracking and sales estimates at roughly $9-$1,200/month, and Motion analyses your own ad accounts. Transcripts can legally be pulled only for content you own or have rights to: the YouTube Data API captions.download works only on videos you can edit, TikTok offers no caption export for others' videos, and Whisper/Descript transcribe your own footage cheaply (~$0.003-0.006/min API). The right method is to tag dozens of winning ads by hook, angle, format, length and CTA, find the repeating pattern, then write ORIGINAL scripts on proven frameworks (hooks in 1-3 s, PAS, BAB, AIDA, UGC testimonial, demo) and test hook variants. Copying scripts verbatim, reusing others' footage/music, fake or AI testimonials (FTC rule, civil penalties ~$51k+ per violation), undisclosed affiliate links, and platform-restricted claims (body before/after, personal attributes) are off limits; Spark Ads/partnership ads are the legitimate way to run another creator's video.
summaries.m5_compare: Every undercut decision reduces to one calculation: landed cost + shipping + platform fees + returns + ad cost must leave a margin at a price below the competitor's effective price. Platform take rates in 2026 are roughly: Amazon 15% referral + FBA fee (~$3-4 small items), TikTok Shop 6% (an 8% rise reported Aug 2026, unverified) plus the creator commission you set (often 10-20%), Etsy ~10-12% all-in, eBay 13.6% + $0.40, Shopify 2.9% + $0.30 plus a plan fee, Walmart 6-20%. Suppliers with APIs (CJ, Printful, Printify, AliExpress Open Platform) let an agent compute landed cost automatically, and Keepa's API is the best automated source for competitor price history; China-sourced goods now pay duties because the $800 de minimis ended. Break-even ROAS = 1 / contribution margin %, and the minimum viable price is C_fixed / (1 - percentage costs - target margin). If you cannot get to that price, undercut on offer (bundle, speed, guarantee) or take the affiliate route instead, and never resell trademarked brands without authorization.
summaries.m6_pipeline: A weekly n8n-orchestrated pipeline can run the research with Google Sheets as the datastore and Claude for normalization and script drafting, at roughly $5-60/month in tools plus optional Keepa/Kalodata subscriptions. Official APIs cover search demand (YouTube, Google Ads keyword ideas, Google Trends alpha), prices/fees (Amazon Creators API, SP-API fees, eBay Browse, SerpApi, Keepa) and EU-only ad libraries (Meta, TikTok), but the highest-signal sources for US short-form ads and TikTok Shop products (TikTok Creative Center, Meta Ad Library UI for US commercial ads, Kalodata/FastMoss) have no open API and need a 15-30 minute manual export or Apify scrapers that conflict with platform ToS. The scoring model weights demand growth 30%, margin/commission 25%, competition 20%, ad saturation 15%, affiliate availability 10%, with hard gates and an undercut formula that subtracts fees, CPA and returns. Humans must set up accounts and API approvals once, approve every 'sell' decision and every script (FTC disclosure, claims, originality) before hand-off to posting automation.
